newsitem.title: USA: Citibank forms global markets unit.
newsitem.headline: Citibank forms global markets unit.

text.p: Citibank, the banking unit of Citicorp, said it formed a new global markets unit within its Global Corporate Banking business.
Citibank said the new unit brings together the former capital markets and trading, corporate finance and cross-border finance groups under a single product management.

"We plan to focus our attention on the growing set of global investors who, like issuers, value our global capabilities, and who want access to the type of investments we naturally originate from our target issuer customer base," said Robert McCormack, executive vice president of Citibank's business with multinational companies.

Citibank said Ernst Brutsche will be responsible for overall implementation of the strategy, focusing on alignment of underlying functions that support the business including risk management, operations and technology, financial control, legal, human resources and marketing and admnistration.

Citibank said formation of the unit would make it possible to provide "a single window of access" to investors in five areas, including cross-border investments from emerging market issuers, higher yielding investments from OECD (Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development) issuers, structured financings from OECD and emerging market issuers, risk management and derivatives, and local currency investments from the emerging markets.
Other executives with key responsibilities in the new unit are Alan MacDonald, Dipak Rastogi and Julian Simmonds.
